sections.text: A hardware trojan is malicious circuitry or a malicious modification inserted during design or fabrication. It may stay dormant until a trigger, then leak data or disable a function. Detection is hard because it may affect very few gates. Secure boot starts from an immutable root of trust and verifies each boot stage with signatures before execution. A trusted execution environment (TEE) isolates sensitive code in a protected area, but its guarantees depend on the implementation and on side-channel resistance.

sections.heading: PUFs and evaluation
sections.text: A physical unclonable function (PUF) derives a device-specific response from manufacturing variation, useful for key generation or identity. Countermeasures must be layered: authenticated boot, memory protection, leakage reduction, tamper detection and supply-chain controls. Security evaluation uses threat modelling, penetration testing, leakage assessment and formal verification. Standards and certification schemes differ by country and sector; check the current official scheme rather than assuming one universal rule.

keyPoints: A threat model defines attacker powers, goals and knowledge before countermeasures are chosen.
Side-channel attacks exploit timing, power, electromagnetic or cache leakage; masking, hiding and constant-time code reduce it.
Hardware trojans are malicious design or fabrication changes, often dormant and hard to detect.
Secure boot verifies each boot stage from an immutable root of trust; a TEE isolates code but is not automatically side-channel safe.
PUFs use manufacturing variation for device identity or key material.
Evaluation combines threat modelling, penetration testing, leakage assessment and formal methods; certification rules vary by country.

en.title: Edge AI and embedded machine learning
en.short: Compression, quantisation, accelerators, co-design and deployment of ML on constrained devices.

sections.heading: Compression and quantisation
sections.text:
Edge AI runs inference on devices with limited memory, energy and compute, such as microcontrollers and embedded boards. Model compression reduces size and cost. Pruning removes weights or channels that contribute little; unstructured pruning gives sparse matrices, while structured pruning removes filters and maps better to hardware. Knowledge distillation trains a small student model to imitate a larger teacher.

Quantisation stores weights and activations in fewer bits, usually int8 instead of float32. Symmetric quantisation uses q = round(x ÷ S), with S = max|x| ÷ 127 for signed int8; dequantise as x ≈ S q. Asymmetric quantisation adds a zero point: q = round(x ÷ S + Z). Post-training quantisation is simple but can lose accuracy; quantisation-aware training models rounding during training.

Example: weights range from −1.2 to 0.8. S = 1.2 ÷ 127 = 0.009449. For x = 0.5, q = round(0.5 ÷ 0.009449) = 53. Dequantised value = 53 × 0.009449 = 0.5008.

sections.heading: Accelerators and co-design
sections.text:
Neural network accelerators speed up multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations. A systolic array passes data between processing elements to reuse weights and activations. DSPs, SIMD units, NPUs (neural processing units) and FPGAs trade flexibility against efficiency. The memory hierarchy often limits performance more than arithmetic, so tiling and layer fusion (combining layers) keep data on chip.

Hardware-software co-design chooses precision, data layout, operator support and scheduling together. A compiler maps layers to supported instructions; unsupported operators fall back to slow software. Designers may change the model, for example replacing an operator, to fit the target.

sections.heading: Benchmarking and deployment
sections.text:
Benchmark on the real device with representative inputs. Report latency, throughput, energy per inference, peak memory and accuracy, plus batch size, precision and clock settings. A model that is small in bytes can still be slow if it has many sequential operations.

Deployment uses runtimes such as TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers or vendor NPU toolchains. Validate accuracy after conversion, test corner cases and monitor drift, meaning accuracy loss as input data changes. Safety-critical deployment may need standards and professional sign-off; these differ by country.

keyPoints: Pruning removes weights or channels; structured pruning suits hardware better.
Quantisation maps floats to low-bit integers using a scale and often a zero point.
Symmetric int8 quantisation uses S = max|x| ÷ 127 and x ≈ S q.
Accelerators such as systolic arrays and NPUs speed MAC operations, but memory often limits them.
Co-design matches model precision, layout and operators to the target hardware.
Benchmark latency, energy, memory and accuracy on the real device with representative data.

en.title: Research methods in computer engineering
en.short: Research questions, literature review, experiments, simulation, reproducibility, ethics and dissertation writing.

sections.heading: Questions and literature
sections.text:
A research question states what you will find out, for whom and under what conditions. A good one is answerable, specific and feasible. Turn a broad interest into a question such as: how does cache size affect energy use for a given workload? State hypotheses and the evidence that would support or reject them.

A literature review is a structured search and critical summary of existing work, not a list. Define search terms, databases and inclusion rules. Read primary sources, record methods and results, and identify gaps your question addresses. Cite accurately.

sections.heading: Experiments and measurement
sections.text: Experimental design plans treatments, controls and repetitions so that effects can be attributed to causes. Define independent variables you change, dependent variables you measure, and nuisance variables you hold constant or randomise. Use pilot runs to size the experiment. Measurement needs units, resolution, calibration and an error model. Report uncertainty, not just a mean. Distinguish internal validity (the experiment supports the claim) from external validity (the result generalises).

sections.heading: Simulation, benchmarking, reproducibility
sections.text: Simulation replaces a system with a model, such as a network or processor model. Validate the model against measurements before trusting predictions. Benchmarking compares systems on agreed workloads and metrics. Report hardware, software versions, input sizes and warm-up. Example: if a baseline takes 120 ms and a new method takes 80 ms, speedup = 120 ÷ 80 = 1.5. Reproducibility means another researcher can repeat the method and obtain consistent results. Share code, data, scripts and parameter files where ethics and licences allow.

sections.heading: Ethics and dissertation
sections.text: Research ethics covers honesty, consent, privacy, safety and fair credit. Experiments on people or personal data usually need approval from an institutional ethics committee; data protection rules differ by country, so check the current local and institutional requirements. Avoid fabrication, plagiarism and undisclosed conflicts. A dissertation presents the question, review, method, results, discussion and limitations in a clear argument. Write for a reader who must be able to repeat your work.

keyPoints: Turn a broad topic into a specific, answerable research question with stated hypotheses.
A literature review is a critical, reproducible search that identifies a gap, not a list of papers.
Define independent, dependent and nuisance variables, and report measurement uncertainty.
Validate a simulation against real measurements before using it for predictions.
Speedup = baseline time ÷ new time; report workloads, hardware and software versions.
Reproducibility requires shared code, data and parameters; ethics approval and data rules vary by country and institution.
